dedupe_keys.name: nature based solutions against floods and droughts in the serchio river basin and massaciuccoli lake phusicos

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes an integrated system of nature-based solutions in the Serchio river basin around Massaciuccoli Lake, near Vecchiano and Pisa in Tuscany, Italy, a shallow coastal lake of 7 square kilometres surrounded by marshes that suffers from agricultural drainage, nutrient inflow, soil erosion, floods and droughts. Measures include a 45-hectare phyto-depuration wetland, of which 15 hectares were built and active, designed to treat about 135,000 cubic metres of water a day, vegetated buffer strips along the secondary canals, conservation agriculture tested on about 60 hectares at two farms, and a 4-hectare sedimentation basin before the pumping station. Most were implemented in the EU Horizon 2020 PHUSICOS project (2018-2023), which used a participatory living lab with the Northern Apennines District Basin Authority and local stakeholders. The page, published in 2022 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the PHUSICOS and CORDIS project pages. Caveats: benefits for flood and drought risk are expected, not measured, costs are not given, and part of the works was still under construction when written. It illustrates nature-based hazard reduction and climate adaptation of drainage and water systems in farmland; related records are GLWD v2, the Room for the River Regge case study and the Watermachine Kristalbad case study.
name: Nature-based solutions against floods and droughts in the Serchio river basin and Massaciuccoli Lake (PHUSICOS)
outcomes: A phyto-depuration wetland and associated nature-based measures were partly built to cut pollutant loads and soil erosion and to buffer floods and droughts around the lake.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study based on EEA Report 1/2021 and the PHUSICOS project
